headline: Highest risk is Cursor’s broad filesystem/network/tool access; the pair otherwise has no documented direct interaction and the course profile is non-runnable.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can read workspace files, clipboard contents, and use MCP, so if the course content is manually copied into Cursor or bridged through files, prompt injection is possible. The zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and exposes no output channel, so there is no documented automatic bridge; uncertainty keeps this above none but below medium.
conditions: IF course text is copied into Cursor buffers or workspace files
IF an MCP server or local file bridge is used to pass zoomcamp content into Cursor
mitigations: Avoid pasting untrusted course text into agent prompts
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task
Keep course materials in a separate read-only folder
Review any copied snippets before asking Cursor to act on them

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents and can egress to model providers, while the zoomcamp profile has no data classes touched and no runtime surfaces. There is no evidence of shared sensitive data with the course profile, so leakage is limited to unusual local copying or workspace sharing rather than a default pairwise leak.
conditions: IF sensitive files are opened in Cursor and then copied into course-related artifacts
IF both profiles are placed in the same shared workspace with readable files
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Use separate OS accounts or directories
Turn off clipboard sharing between tools
Audit what Cursor can read before opening secrets

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has broad write, shell, git, and network capabilities, but the zoomcamp profile is not runnable and has no write or network capabilities of its own. That makes direct capability conflict unlikely; any conflict would require the course materials to be wrapped in another runnable agent or external automation not shown here.
conditions: IF the zoomcamp content is embedded in a separate runnable wrapper with write access
IF Cursor and another tool are both pointed at the same mutable repo
mitigations: Do not run multiple writers on the same directory
Use git branches for any edits Cursor makes
Pause automation before manual course updates
Keep the course repo read-only when not editing

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code or edits that a user may apply to course materials, but the zoomcamp profile is a static course and does not itself act on Cursor output. There is no documented downstream automation from B, so the main risk is mistaken human reliance on Cursor output rather than an autonomous cascade.
conditions: IF a human copies Cursor output into course notes or assignments without review
IF another automation consumes Cursor output as authoritative
mitigations: Verify generated code or notes before reuse
Require a second review for any copied output
Keep Cursor output in draft-only files
Do not auto-apply edits from the agent

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: Cursor’s profile mentions general model-provider API keys and local editor use, while the zoomcamp profile is a non-runnable open-source course with no data residency, retention, or regulated-data handling fields. Because the relevant compliance surfaces are absent in B, there is no documented pairwise compliance pathway to cite beyond the profiles themselves.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Cursor workflows
IF a separate deployment adds residency or retention constraints not shown here
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in the course workspace
Review any external service settings before use
Keep the course repo free of secrets
Document retention settings if new data classes are added
